title: Cross-Platform Cloud Benchmark Reveals Wide Gap Between Physical Qubit Counts and Entangled GHZ State Sizes - Quantum Computing Report
gist: A Spanish consortium (Gradiant, UPV/EHU, BCAM and partners) benchmarked nine cloud-accessible quantum processors from five vendors on GHZ-state generation with no error mitigation, finding large superconducting chips sustain genuine multipartite entanglement over less than a quarter of their physical qubits, while a 12-qubit AQT trapped-ion device used 100% of its register. Median calibration metrics proved poor predictors of multi-qubit performance.

insights.claim: An out-of-the-box cloud GHZ-state benchmark of nine quantum processors found large superconducting devices maintain multipartite entanglement across less than a quarter of their physical qubit registers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Headline physical qubit counts overstate usable entangled capacity; discount vendor qubit-count marketing.
insights.locator: A Spanish research consortium led by Gradiant

insights.claim: IBM Phoenix (Nighthawk r2, 120 qubits) achieved the largest passing GHZ state in the cloud benchmark at 27 qubits (23% register utilization, 3.0% per-qubit GHZ error), ahead of IBM Basquecountry (Heron r2, 156 qubits) at 24 qubits and IBM Pittsburgh (Heron r3, 156 qubits) at 21.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's newer Nighthawk square-lattice chip outperformed its larger Heron heavy-hex chips — topology matters more than size.

insights.claim: The 12-qubit AQT IBEX Q1 trapped-ion processor with all-to-all connectivity achieved a GHZ state across 100% of its register with the lowest per-qubit GHZ error (2.8%) and the highest fidelity witness (Y = 0.711) among the nine tested cloud backends.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Trapped-ion all-to-all connectivity delivers far higher register utilization than superconducting chips — a quality-over-quantity signal for ion players.

insights.claim: Rigetti's 107-qubit Cepheus-1 chiplet processor reached only a 4-qubit passing GHZ state (4% utilization, 16.3% per-qubit error) and the CESGA Qmio/OQC 32-qubit Coaxmon device only 3 qubits (20.0% error) in an unmitigated cloud GHZ benchmark.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Rigetti and OQC lagged peers badly on default-cloud entanglement — a negative datapoint for their competitive positioning.

insights.claim: IQM's smaller processors showed higher register utilization than IBM's large chips in the cloud GHZ benchmark: IQM Garnet (20 qubits) reached 13-qubit GHZ (65%) and IQM Emerald (54 qubits) reached 20 qubits (37%), though with higher per-qubit errors of 6.2% and 4.2%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Mid-size devices can utilize registers more fully, but per-qubit error still trails IBM's best chips.

insights.claim: The GHZ benchmark used the QuSquare suite's multipartite entanglement protocol with Direct Fidelity Estimation over 2,952 randomly sampled stabilizers per circuit size, accessing processors via IBM Quantum Platform, Amazon Braket, and the Galicia Supercomputing Center (CESGA).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Independent, cross-cloud, open benchmarks are emerging as a check on vendor-reported performance.

insights.claim: Prior single-vendor demonstrations reporting larger entangled GHZ states relied on custom pulse compilation, post-selection, and readout mitigation, whereas typical cloud users with default compilation and no error mitigation see much smaller entangled states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vendor hero results are not what cloud customers experience; diligence should ask for default-workflow benchmarks.

insights.claim: Quantum entanglement benchmark rankings depend heavily on the statistical decision rule: all nine devices passed a non-exclusion GME threshold at some size, but strict certification (Y − ε ≥ 0.5) left only four — IBM Phoenix, IBM Basquecountry, AQT IBEX Q1 and IQM Garnet.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Check which statistical criterion a benchmark uses before comparing vendors' entanglement claims.

insights.claim: Median calibration metrics are unreliable predictors of multi-qubit performance: on superconducting backends, effective per-qubit GHZ error rates exceeded median two-qubit gate errors by roughly one order of magnitude.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Spec-sheet two-qubit fidelities understate real-workload error ~10x; adjust timelines for useful advantage accordingly.
insights.quote: median calibration metrics are unreliable predictors of multi-qubit performance
insights.locator: Comparing hardware specifications against observed fidelities

insights.claim: The order-of-magnitude gap between superconducting spec-sheet gate errors and observed GHZ errors is attributed to unmitigated readout errors, idling decoherence, crosstalk, and compiler qubit-chain selection.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Software/compiler and readout improvements may unlock more value than raw qubit additions — watch tooling vendors.
insights.locator: Comparing hardware specifications against observed fidelities
